reasons: The AUDIT rule constrains a Vendor-side right that burdens the Customer; the document contains no audit, inspection, verification or record-keeping obligation on the Customer, so our exposure is nil — at least as favourable as the preferred position and clear of every walk-away trigger.

Correctly classified as compliant rather than 'missing': the rule does not expect a Customer-protective clause we lack; inserting audit machinery would create a Vendor right that does not exist and worsen our position.

No redline and no counterparty comment is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered p0001 is unchanged and the cited text (ordinary cooperation for service delivery) is accurately characterised as not an audit right.
The failed deterministic 'audit frequency limited' check is explained and non-probative here — there is no audit clause to bear a frequency cap.
Rationale appropriately logs the forward-looking watch item (Exhibits could later introduce Customer reporting or fee true-ups) as a note rather than a flagged deviation.
